doc: RETENTION-1 (2026-11-16): every table the tick worker creates is listed here. A table with keep_days is pruned once a day by seed/worker/src/retention.js (rows whose time column is older than keep_days, at most max_rows_per_run per table per day); a table marked keep: state holds current state, not history, and is never pruned. test/plan-limits.test.mjs fails when a migration or the worker creates a table that is not listed. Lesson from the fleet this org was split from: its audit database reached 1,011 tables, 266 of them backup copies never removed, and append-only ledgers kept every row forever. Windows: criticality reads 14 days (seed/autonomy/criticality.json window_days); the trust ledger reads every outcome, so outcomes are kept a year.

free_tier_samples.reason: FREE-TIER-1: hourly account-wide usage samples; the tick reads the latest two hours

host_events.reason: HOSTS-1: one row per hosting action or inbound hosting event; deploy status and stall detection read the last day, so 30 days is ample

airouter_cache.reason: AI-ROUTER-1: cached model replies, pruned by core/airouter (7 days)

airouter_calls.reason: AI-ROUTER-1: one row per model call, pruned by core/airouter (30 days); integer-millisecond time column, so retention.js cannot prune it

airouter_stats.reason: AI-ROUTER-1: one row per kind and model, the routing memory

airouter_retired.reason: AIROUTER-NO-RUN-1: one row per model the platform reported as deprecated; read with a 7 day window, at most one row per model

social_posted.reason: REACH-1: one row per post and channel; the publisher reads this week, the reach loop reads a year

human_inbox.reason: SOCIAL-MODULE-1: public replies and mentions with the author hashed; read while they are new, never needed after a quarter

_migrations.reason: which migrations have been applied; a record of schema state, never history to prune

hits.reason: pruned by seed/analytics/analytics.js (35 days raw, 2 days self-check rows)

analytics_meta.reason: analytics settings and the report cache

items.reason: the work queue and its dispositions (the no-silent-drop record)

claims.reason: live claims; released claims are deleted by the claim reaper

trust_ledger.reason: one row per surface and action class

handoffs.reason: one row per handed-off pull request

audit_log.reason: AUDIT-CHAIN-1: sealed into archive segments after 7 days by seed/worker/src/auditchain.js

audit_segments.reason: one row per sealed segment (about one a day): the index and hash chain of the archive

live_changes.reason: LIVE-FRESH-1: merged PRs cached for the public changelog; the page shows 14 days and the table also keeps the newest 400 rows

live_changes_meta.reason: LIVE-FRESH-1: one row per repository, rewritten every pass

decision_log.reason: DECISIONS-1: one row per Worker-side decision (AI router model pick, free-tier governor level) with its metric, prediction and outcome; the public page reads 7 days, older rows are hash-chained archives

goal_samples.reason: GOALS-1: one reading per goal per tick for the trend line; the page shows 14 days

goal_adjustments.reason: GOALS-1: every knob change with its prediction and verdict; each is also a hash-chained audit row

goals.reason: GOALS-1: one row per goal; retired goals stay so a goal's history is never lost

goal_knobs.reason: GOALS-1: one row per knob with its current value; bounded by the tenant limit of 80

stickiness_state.reason: STICKY-1: one row per system, rewritten every pass by the tick step stickiness

stickiness_series.reason: STICKY-1: one row per system per day; the step itself deletes rows older than 400 days

progress_cadence.reason: PROGRESS-1: one row per system, rewritten every pass by the tick step progress

trust_ledger_backup_0027.reason: OL-20261118-4: one-time copy of trust_ledger taken by migration 0027 before the key rebuild; one row per surface and action class, never written again

trust_ledger_v2.reason: OL-20261118-4: exists only inside migration 0027's batch and is renamed to trust_ledger before the batch ends

cf_alerts.reason: CF-ALERTS-1: one row per Cloudflare alert; settling reads the last day per type, so 30 days is ample

kg_nodes.reason: DATAGRAPH-1: one row per record of the system's own data; bi-temporal (valid_to closes a row that left the data), bounded by max_rows_total per pass

kg_edges.reason: DATAGRAPH-1: one row per connection between records, bounded by the nodes; proposed leads are settled kept or rejected within 14 days

kg_insights.reason: DATAGRAPH-1: current insights only; each pass rewrites them and deletes the ones that no longer fire

kg_runs.reason: DATAGRAPH-1: one row per graph pass, pruned to 400 days by seed/worker/src/datagraph.js

kg_vec.reason: KGRAPH-AI-1: one embedding per live graph node, rewritten when the node changes

kg_summaries.reason: KGRAPH-AI-1: one summary per community insight

kg_cost.reason: KGRAPH-AI-1: one row per day of graph AI cost

kg_sources.reason: Tenant engine seed/worker/src/knowledge.js (DATAGRAPH-1 built rows): one hash per source record; retired rows pruned after retain_days by runKg

kg_state.reason: Tenant engine seed/worker/src/knowledge.js: a handful of keys per tenant (last analysis, kind weights)

directory_registration.reason: DISCOVER-1 / BOOT-4: one row (id 1), the directory's last answer to this system's registration
